title: Marketing Campaign Analysis
findings: 14.7% of cellular records and 5.2% of telephone records ended in subscription.
Records with prior campaign success have 65.1% subscription rate (1,373 records).
Overall, 4,640 of 41,188 records indicate a term-deposit subscription.
action: Use the differences to design a prospective, randomized channel or contact-strategy test, recording costs, eligibility and incremental subscriptions.
problem: How do observed term-deposit subscription rates differ across bank telemarketing records?
grain: One campaign example in the bank-additional-full.csv sample of a Portuguese bank, May 2008 to November 2010. Multiple contacts can be required for one client.
definitions: Subscription rate = records with y = yes ÷ all records in the segment.
Contact is the recorded communication type; campaign counts contacts for the client during the current campaign.
Previous outcome describes the previous campaign and includes a nonexistent category.
Rates are record-weighted; without customer IDs, unique customers and independent customer-level conversion cannot be calculated.
caveats: The source records phone campaigns, not paid search or social. It has no spend, revenue, cost or randomized assignment: CPA, ROAS and incremental effect cannot be computed. Channel and previous-campaign comparisons are observational and may reflect targeting or economic conditions. Last-call duration is known only after a call and must not be used for pre-call targeting. The data is historical.
nextsteps: Check campaign eligibility and contact histories before comparing audience groups.
Avoid using call duration as a predictor before the call; review sensitive attributes and fair treatment.
Randomize a channel strategy and collect spend and margin before estimating incremental ROI.
quality: 41,188 campaign records; 0 blank cells; 12,718 source values labeled unknown. 12 identical-looking rows retained because there is no customer ID or event ID.
citation: Moro, S., Rita, P., & Cortez, P. (2014), Bank Marketing, UCI Machine Learning Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5K306 (CC BY 4.0).
